papers_read.title_as_printed: Cross-lingual detection of mild cognitive impairment based on temporal parameters of spontaneous speech (Gosztolya et al., Computer Speech & Language 69 (2021) 101215)
Detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment From Non-Semantic, Acoustic Voice Features: The Framingham Heart Study (Ding et al., JMIR Aging 2024;7:e55126)

what_each_reports.P-58: SVM on 15 ASR-derived temporal/pause parameters from a telephone 'previous day' monologue, speaker-wise nested leave-one-out CV, MCI vs HC in two separate samples of 33 (English: 14 MCI/19 HC, New York; Hungarian: 13 MCI/20 HC, Szeged). All-features monolingual: English accuracy 84.8%, AUC 0.932; Hungarian accuracy 75.8%, AUC 0.727. Best subset (filler-related, Hungarian) accuracy 90.9%, AUC 0.912 (0.923 with English ASR). Across all feature subsets AUC ranges 0.519-0.932. The abstract's '67-92%' is a range over several metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, specificity) across subsets, not an accuracy range. No confidence intervals.
what_each_reports.P-167: Random forest on 29 selected OpenSMILE/Praat acoustic features from diarized participant speech during Framingham Heart Study neuropsychological testing, 10-fold CV, 100 MCI vs 100 age/sex/education-matched CN: AUC 0.87 (95% CI 0.81-0.94); shorter recordings AUC 0.79-0.82.

quantity_a: Cross-validated discrimination (accuracy and other EER-threshold metrics, AUC) of an SVM on temporal speech parameters for Petersen-criteria MCI vs HC, two memory-clinic samples of 33 (English, Hungarian), telephone spontaneous monologue
quantity_b: 10-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC of a random forest on 29 non-semantic acoustic features for DSM-IV/NINCDS-ADRDA panel-diagnosed MCI vs CN, 200 community-cohort (FHS) participants, speech recorded during NP testing
incompatible_if_same: No. P-167's AUC 0.87 (95% CI 0.81-0.94) lies inside P-58's own range of AUCs across feature sets (0.727-0.932 for the all-feature models) and its CI includes P-58's English all-feature AUC 0.932. The record's claim_a is a mixed-metric range, not a single estimate, and neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match: both MCI vs cognitively normal detection (T1)
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: P-58 uses its own New York (Columbia) and Szeged memory-clinic cohorts; P-167 uses the Framingham Heart Study community cohort. The record's dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong; no waiver on record
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal cross-validation only (nested LOO vs 10-fold), no external cohort

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as recorded: claim_a is a range over several metric types (accuracy, precision, recall, specificity), claim_b is a ROC-AUC. On AUC alone the two overlap.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither paper is flagged and no figure reaches 0.97; it is a cross-cohort performance comparison
independence: Independent studies: different groups (Szeged/Columbia vs Boston University/FHS), different cohorts, no shared authors.
grounds: P-58's '67-92%' is a range of several metrics across feature subsets, not a single estimate, so it cannot contradict one AUC.
P-167's AUC 0.87 (95% CI 0.81-0.94) overlaps P-58's reported AUCs (0.727 Hungarian, 0.932 English all-feature models), so the results are compatible.
Two methods on two cohorts each report a score and neither claims an ordering the other refutes, which the rule reads as not incompatible.
Independently of this, the dataset-family gate fails (memory-clinic samples in New York/Szeged vs the Framingham community cohort) with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: the language on which the ASR system was trained only slightly affects the MCI classification performance, because we got quite similar scores (67-92%) as we did in the monolingual cases (67-92% as well).
Both the English-speaking (n = 33; New York, NY, USA) and the Hungarian-speaking (n = 33; Szeged, Hungary) participants were diagnosed as MCI or HC.
the AUC and minCllr values are also quite good (0.932 and 0.305, respectively)
for Hungarian, the classification performance was acceptable (with classification metrics falling into the range 66.776.9% and with an AUC value of 0.727). [extract drops the dash: read 66.7-76.9%]
An optimal subset of 29 features was identified that resulted in an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.87, with a 95% CI of 0.81-0.94.
a case-control data set was created consisting of 100 MCI cases and 100 cognitively normal (CN) controls and matched on age, sex, and education

record_defects: dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong: P-58 uses its own New York and Szeged cohorts, P-167 the Framingham Heart Study.
claim_a 'P-58: 67-92% range on T1' presents a mixed-metric range across feature subsets as a performance result; it is not an accuracy range.
P-58 registry Best_Metric 'Acc 92' is not an accuracy the paper reports: the highest accuracy is 90.9% (filler-related, Hungarian); 92.3% is a recall value.
P-167 registry Dataset 'not reported' is wrong: the paper names the Framingham Heart Study.

resolution 'Rejected - false positive' conflicts with resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate'; the 'bridging evidence' list (e.g. P-422, P-478, P-538) cites non-speech studies and names no condition separating the two results.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only a restatement of the pair as a single matched quantity (e.g. P-58's all-feature English AUC 0.932 vs P-167's 0.87) with a waiver of the dataset-family gate; even then the P-167 confidence interval (0.81-0.94) includes 0.932, so the results would remain compatible.
